content.text:
**T-6004 has been escalated.** Here's a summary of what I did and why:

---

### Summary

I read the ticket, listed pods in the `messaging` namespace, and checked the pod details for `rabbitmq-1`. I found:

- **Root cause of the stuck pod:** Node `ip-10-0-52-17.ec2.internal` is unresponsive (`NodeLost`), causing `rabbitmq-1` to be stuck in `Terminating`. This is expected Kubernetes behavior — pods on unreachable nodes are not automatically deleted [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#delete-pods-1].
- **Why force-delete is unsafe right now:** The pod's `data-rabbitmq-1` PVC uses `ReadWriteOnce` and is **still volume-attached to the lost node**. Force-deleting without first confirming the EC2 instance is terminated could result in two RabbitMQ pods writing to the same EBS volume simultaneously, risking **data corruption and quorum breakage** [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#force-deletion-0].
- **Safe path:** The platform team must first terminate (or confirm the termination of) the EC2 instance via AWS and then delete the Node object from the Kubernetes API. Only then can a force-delete (or automatic cleanup) safely proceed [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#delete-pods-2]. Since this requires AWS console access that neither the ticket owner nor I have, I escalated to the platform team.
